7-1.title: Capitalization Rules
7-1.learn:
HOW TO CAPITALIZE CORRECTLY

Capitalize these:
- The FIRST word of every sentence.
- The pronoun 'I' (always).
- PROPER NOUNS — specific names of people (Maria), places (Miami), days (Monday), months (June), holidays (Thanksgiving), and titles (President Lincoln).

Do NOT capitalize common nouns (city, girl, month) unless they begin a sentence.

Example 1 — 'On Monday, Maria visited Miami.'
Capitalize 'On' (first word), 'Monday' (day), 'Maria' (person), and 'Miami' (place).

Example 2 — Common vs. proper: 'I want to visit a city' (common, lowercase) vs. 'I want to visit Orlando' (proper, capital).

Example 3 — Seasons are NOT capitalized: 'I love summer.' But months ARE: 'I love July.'
Tip: Ask 'Is this the SPECIFIC name of one particular person, place, or thing?' If yes, capitalize it.

questions.question: Which sentence is capitalized correctly?
questions.explanation: Capitalize the first word 'My' and the proper noun 'Florida.'

questions.question: Which word should always be capitalized?
questions.explanation: The pronoun 'I' is always capitalized.

questions.question: Which word is a proper noun that needs a capital letter?
questions.explanation: 'Tuesday' is the specific name of a day, so it is a proper noun and is capitalized.

questions.question: Which sentence is capitalized correctly?

choices.A: We visited the Grand Canyon in April.
choices.B: we visited the grand canyon in april.
choices.C: We visited the grand Canyon in April.
choices.D: We Visited the Grand Canyon in april.

questions.explanation: Capitalize the first word, the proper place 'Grand Canyon,' and the month 'April.'

questions.question: Which word should NOT be capitalized in the middle of a sentence?
questions.explanation: 'Girl' is a common noun, so it stays lowercase unless it starts a sentence.

questions.question: Which sentence is capitalized correctly?
questions.explanation: Capitalize 'On' (first word) and 'Thanksgiving' (holiday), but 'turkey' the food is a common noun.

questions.question: Which word is correctly NOT capitalized?
questions.explanation: Seasons like 'spring' are common nouns and stay lowercase; months, places, and days are proper nouns.

questions.question: Which sentence has a capitalization ERROR?

choices.A: We drove to Texas last June.
choices.B: My dog Rex loves the Park.
choices.D: I read a book about Egypt.

questions.explanation: 'Park' is a common noun here and should be lowercase: 'My dog Rex loves the park.'

questions.question: Which sentence is capitalized correctly?

choices.A: principal Jones spoke to our class on wednesday.
choices.B: Principal Jones spoke to our Class on Wednesday.
choices.C: Principal Jones spoke to our class on Wednesday.
choices.D: principal jones spoke to our class on wednesday.

questions.explanation: Capitalize the title with the name ('Principal Jones') and the day 'Wednesday,' but 'class' is a common noun.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly capitalizes a title used with a name versus a common noun?

choices.A: I asked President Lincoln a question, but no other president answered.
choices.B: I asked president Lincoln a question, but no other President answered.
choices.C: I asked President lincoln a question, but no other president answered.
choices.D: I asked president lincoln a question, but no other President answered.

questions.explanation: 'President Lincoln' is a title with a name (capitalized), but 'president' alone is a common noun (lowercase).

7-2.title: Capitalizing Titles
7-2.learn:
HOW TO CAPITALIZE TITLES

In titles of books, movies, and songs:
- Capitalize the FIRST and LAST words, no matter what.
- Capitalize all IMPORTANT words (nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, pronouns).
- Leave LITTLE words lowercase in the middle: a, an, the, and, but, or, of, to, in, for (articles, short conjunctions, and short prepositions) — UNLESS they are the first or last word.

Example 1 — 'The Lord of the Rings.'
'The' is capitalized because it is first. 'Lord' and 'Rings' are important words. 'of' and 'the' in the middle stay lowercase.

Example 2 — 'Charlie and the Chocolate Factory.'
'Charlie,' 'Chocolate,' and 'Factory' are important. 'and' and 'the' in the middle are lowercase.

Example 3 — 'Gone with the Wind.'
'Gone' (first) and 'Wind' (last) are capitalized; 'with' and 'the' in the middle stay lowercase.
Tip: Always capitalize the first and last words, then capitalize everything except little linking words in between.

questions.question: Which title is capitalized correctly?
questions.explanation: Capitalize the first word, last word, and important words; little words 'in' and 'the' in the middle stay lowercase.

questions.question: In a title, which words should always be capitalized?
questions.explanation: The first and last words of a title are always capitalized, no matter what.

questions.question: Which little word stays lowercase in the middle of a title?
questions.explanation: 'The' is a small article that stays lowercase in the middle of a title.

questions.question: Which title is capitalized correctly?
questions.explanation: Important words are capitalized, while 'and' and 'the' in the middle stay lowercase.

questions.question: Which title is capitalized correctly?
questions.explanation: 'Gone' (first) and 'Wind' (last) are capitalized; 'with' and 'the' in the middle stay lowercase.

questions.question: Why is 'of' lowercase in 'The Wizard of Oz'?

choices.A: It is a little linking word in the middle of the title.

questions.explanation: Short prepositions like 'of' stay lowercase when they fall in the middle of a title.

questions.question: Which title is capitalized correctly?
questions.explanation: Important words are capitalized; 'of' and 'a' in the middle stay lowercase.

questions.question: Which title has a capitalization ERROR?

choices.A: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
choices.B: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire

questions.explanation: 'And' is a small conjunction in the middle and should be lowercase: 'Percy Jackson and the Olympians.'

questions.question: Which title is capitalized correctly?
questions.explanation: 'A' is capitalized as the first word, 'Wrinkle' and 'Time' are important, and 'in' in the middle stays lowercase.

questions.question: Which title correctly capitalizes a small word because it is the LAST word?
questions.explanation: 'About' is normally a little word, but as the LAST word of the title it must be capitalized.

7-3.title: Commonly Confused Words
7-3.learn:
HOW TO CHOOSE COMMONLY CONFUSED WORDS

Some words sound alike but mean different things. Learn these pairs:
- THEIR = ownership ('their house'); THERE = a place ('over there'); THEY'RE = 'they are.'
- YOUR = ownership ('your book'); YOU'RE = 'you are.'
- ITS = ownership ('its tail'); IT'S = 'it is.'
- TO = toward/part of a verb ('to school,' 'to run'); TOO = also/very ('me too,' 'too hot'); TWO = the number 2.

Example 1 — 'You're going to love their new house over there.'
'You're' = you are; 'their' = ownership; 'there' = place. All three correct!

Example 2 — Test 'they're': replace it with 'they are.' 'They're late' = 'They are late.' Works, so it's correct.

Example 3 — 'to / too / two': 'I have two tickets, and I want to go too.'
'two' = number, 'to go' = part of the verb, 'too' = also.
Tip: When unsure, try replacing with the long form (they are, you are, it is). If it fits, use the apostrophe version.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: '___ going to be a fun day.'
questions.explanation: 'It's' means 'it is,' which fits: 'It is going to be a fun day.'

questions.question: Choose the correct word: 'Please put the books over ___.'
questions.explanation: 'There' refers to a place, which is what 'over ___' needs.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: 'Is this ___ backpack?'
questions.explanation: 'Your' shows ownership of the backpack; 'you're' would mean 'you are.'

questions.question: Choose the correct word: '___ excited about the trip.'
questions.explanation: 'They're' means 'they are,' which fits: 'They are excited about the trip.'

questions.question: Choose the correct word: 'I have ___ much homework tonight.'
questions.explanation: 'Too' means 'very' or 'excessively,' fitting 'too much homework.'

questions.question: Choose the correct word: 'The team lost ___ first game.'
questions.explanation: 'Its' shows ownership of the game; 'it's' would wrongly mean 'it is.'

questions.question: Choose the correct word: '___ doing a great job on the project.'
questions.explanation: 'You're' means 'you are,' which fits: 'You are doing a great job.'

questions.question: Which sentence uses all the confusing words correctly?

choices.A: Their going to bring they're dog over there.
choices.B: There going to bring their dog over they're.
choices.C: They're going to bring there dog over their.
choices.D: They're going to bring their dog over there.

questions.explanation: 'They're' = they are, 'their' = ownership of the dog, and 'there' = the place.

questions.question: Choose the correct words: 'I want ___ go ___, and I have ___ tickets.'
questions.explanation: 'to go' is part of the verb, 'too' means also, and 'two' is the number.

questions.question: Which sentence is CORRECT?

choices.A: Your the best, and you're project is amazing.
choices.B: You're the best, and your project is amazing.
choices.C: Your the best, and your project is amazing.
choices.D: You're the best, and you're project is amazing.

questions.explanation: 'You're' = you are (the best), and 'your' shows ownership of the project.

7-4.title: Spelling Patterns & Plurals
7-4.learn:
HOW TO SPELL PLURALS CORRECTLY

Most plurals just add -s: cat → cats, book → books.
But some follow special patterns:
- Words ending in -s, -x, -ch, or -sh add -es: box → boxes, wish → wishes, bus → buses, church → churches.
- Words ending in a CONSONANT + y change y to i and add -es: candy → candies, baby → babies. (But VOWEL + y just adds -s: key → keys, day → days.)
- Some words ending in -f or -fe change to -ves: leaf → leaves, knife → knives.
- Irregular plurals change completely: child → children, mouse → mice, foot → feet.

Example 1 — 'wish' ends in -sh, so add -es: 'wishes.'
Example 2 — 'baby' ends in consonant + y, so change y to i and add -es: 'babies.'
Example 3 — 'key' ends in vowel + y, so just add -s: 'keys.'
Tip: Look at the LAST letters first to decide which plural rule to use.

questions.question: What is the plural of 'cat'?
questions.explanation: Most nouns just add -s, so 'cat' becomes 'cats.'

questions.question: What is the plural of 'box'?
questions.explanation: Words ending in -x add -es, so 'box' becomes 'boxes.'

questions.question: What is the plural of 'wish'?
questions.explanation: Words ending in -sh add -es, so 'wish' becomes 'wishes.'

questions.question: What is the plural of 'candy'?
questions.explanation: 'Candy' ends in consonant + y, so change y to i and add -es: 'candies.'

questions.question: What is the plural of 'key'?
questions.explanation: 'Key' ends in vowel + y, so just add -s: 'keys.'

questions.question: What is the plural of 'church'?
questions.explanation: Words ending in -ch add -es, so 'church' becomes 'churches.'

questions.question: What is the plural of 'baby'?
questions.explanation: 'Baby' ends in consonant + y, so change y to i and add -es: 'babies.'

questions.question: What is the plural of 'leaf'?
questions.explanation: Some words ending in -f change to -ves, so 'leaf' becomes 'leaves.'

questions.question: What is the plural of 'mouse'?
questions.explanation: 'Mouse' has an irregular plural that changes completely to 'mice.'

questions.question: Which plural is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: 'Child' has the irregular plural 'children,' not 'childs' or 'childrens.'
